title: Before I formed thee (Jeremiah 1)
hook: a young man says I am a child, and God says I knew thee before

segments.voice: Yesterday, the eved, the servant whose wounds heal others. Your line was by his bruises. A new week, and a new prophet.

He comes from a family of priests in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin. The book dates him from the thirteenth year of King Josiah until Jerusalem is carried away captive. He's young; how young, nobody knows, since the text only lets him call himself a boy. And he's about to be handed a hard job: to tell his own people, year after year, that disaster is coming, to watch them ignore him, and then to watch it happen. His name is Jeremiah, Jeremias in the Douay-Rheims. And it begins with something about before he was born.
screen: `A PRIEST'S SON FROM ANATHOTH.` → `THE THIRTEENTH YEAR OF JOSIAH.` → `A HARD JOB.`

segments.voice: The word of the Lord comes to him, in the Douay-Rheims: "Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee: and before thou camest forth out of the womb, I sanctified thee, and made thee a prophet unto the nations." Notice the order. Known first. Then set apart. Then given a job. Before Jeremiah did anything, he was known. His answer is honest. In the Douay: "Ah, ah, ah, Lord God: behold, I cannot speak, for I am a child." Stammering. God doesn't argue about his age: say not, I am a child. You'll go where I send you. Be not afraid, for I am with thee. Then God touches his mouth, the way the coal touched Isaiah's lips: I have given my words in thy mouth. Then a strange little test. What do you see, Jeremiah? A branch of an almond tree. Good, God says, for I am watching over my word. In Hebrew it's a pun: almond is shaqed, watching is shoqed. Some readers explain the name: the almond wakes early in spring, the watchful tree. The Douay, following the Latin, simply calls it a rod watching. The Church has taken that first line further than Jeremiah's own story: the Catechism quotes it in teaching that human life is to be respected and protected from the moment of conception. For Jeremiah, the knowing came first, before all the hard years.
screen: `KNOWN, SET APART, SENT.` · `AH, AH, AH: I AM A CHILD.` · `I HAVE GIVEN MY WORDS IN THY MOUTH.` · `ALMOND, THE WATCHFUL TREE.` · then, large: `BEFORE I FORMED THEE, I KNEW THEE.`

segments.voice: Set down, one at a time, the things you usually use to explain who you are: your job, your mistakes, your age, what people think of you. Underneath them all, Jeremiah heard something older. If you pray, rest in his line, before I formed thee, I knew thee; if you don't, simply let yourself be for a moment, without needing to earn it.
shaqed. Hebrew for almond, the branch God showed Jeremiah as a sign that he was watching over his word. Today's word.
Your line: known before the womb. Known first, then set apart, then sent. Day four hundred twenty-one.

howItsDone: Catholics hear Jeremiah's call at Mass, and the Catechism cites Jeremiah 1:5 in its teaching on the dignity of human life from conception.

Wait until you're older, and then I'll give you the words to say.

chat.meaning: God doesn't argue about his age. Jeremiah was known first, then set apart and sent, with God's words in his mouth and God beside him.

Josiah.meaning: the king of Judah when Jeremiah's call came

notes: The title follows the KJV wording ('Before I formed thee'), so 1:5 is quoted from the KJV; the Douay reads 'Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee'. Confirm, or swap to the Douay.
Thirteenth year of Josiah (1:2) as about 627/626 BC; confirm 'about 627'.

CCC 2270 quotes Jeremiah 1:5 on respect for human life from conception; confirm. Reviewer removed a sentence that put words in the Catechism's mouth ('every person is known by God before anyone else sees them'); the script now says only what 2270 teaches.
Shaqed / shoqed wordplay (1:11–12): standard; confirm pointing. The almond as the first tree to blossom in the land is a common gloss.
Jeremiah's ministry of about forty years (627 to after 587 BC): confirm 'four decades'.

Editor review (2026-10-01): Jeremiah 1:5 now quoted from the Douay-Rheims instead of the KJV (Catholic path); 1:9 aligned to the Douay ('given'); cut 'a few miles north', 'about 627 BC', 'forty years', 'four decades', 'the hardest job in the Bible', 'the most honest thing' and 'the first tree to wake' (claims rule); the practice no longer states as fact that the listener was known before birth.
